doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: The Rika band and funeral bands
title: Funeral procession order, Celestine and the trombonist Bay Bay Ridgely
summary: Tom and Martin tell how the bands lined up at a graveyard, with Excelsior in front, Tuxedo in the middle and Rika behind, and how Celestine could not be caught. They recall Bay Bay Ridgely on trombone and who played in the Excelsior.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well we opened up, we opened up right at the graveyard you see. I believe we was behind, wasn't we? We was behind. We was the last man. And then we opened up, let them go in the graveyard.
You see how it was, you take, Urico, I mean Excelsior was in front.
Tuxedo in the middle. Yeah. And Excelsior, I mean Ricker was behind, had Celestine between you. Had them all between you, all the head of us. Yeah, Celestine between.
And we opened up and let them go in the graveyard. But afterwards we would look for the band that you was gone. Look at that. Them other band you see and you're going to see.
No, no, Excelsior didn't go to Ricker. Celestine. The, what you call them? Celestine in there. Yeah. Couldn't catch him with a, with a ten foot pull.
Couldn't catch him nowhere. Well you know what, it's what after we get out, you know what it's going to be. Who, who tied the dog? That's right.
That's right. Tuxedo, that's the dog.
Yeah, Tuxedo. You know what he mean in there, he was blowing trambones. He died of them, caught him. Uh, there's a dog fella that's there.
That's it. Bay Bay Ridgely. He used to playing trambones.

Who you was playing with? Yeah. That's what you see there, that's what you see when, when uh. We had, we had Red playing in the carnage up there, didn't we? Yeah. Yeah. We had Red and carnage playing.
Red was on trambones those days, huh? That's right.
Yeah. He was trambones him and carnage.
Yeah. That's right. And then you had, uh, you take, Exelster had, uh, Harrison and Buddy. Harrison, Barnes and Buddy. That's right.
